best_for: Kids, parents and teachers who want to build Scratch projects on a Windows PC or Mac without an internet connection, such as on a classroom laptop with unreliable Wi-Fi.
description:
Scratch is a coding tool for kids in which programs are built from blocks instead of typed code. A team led by Professor Mitchel Resnick created it at the MIT Media Lab in 2007. Since 2019 it has been run by the Scratch Foundation, an independent nonprofit that develops the editor and looks after its online community.

You drag colored blocks and snap them together to bring a story, a game or an animated drawing to life, with no syntax to get wrong. Start with ready-made characters, backdrops and sounds from the library, upload your own pictures, or draw them yourself. Beginner tutorials and starter projects help with the first steps, and you can remix an existing project instead of starting from a blank stage.

points.title: The web editor without the web
points.text: The Scratch app lets you create and save projects offline. It is free, and you can also keep using Scratch in the browser at the same time.

points.title: No sharing from the app
points.text: You cannot share to the Scratch community from the app. Save the project file, upload it to your Scratch account on the website, and share it there.

points.title: Hardware without Scratch Link
points.text: The app connects to extensions such as micro:bit and LEGO Boost directly, so you do not need Scratch Link running.

points.title: Linux is unofficial
points.text: The Scratch team says Linux is not supported. The Flatpak listed here is a community build that Flathub does not mark as verified, and it is still on 3.10.1 while Windows and macOS are on 3.32.1.

points.title: Windows: 32-bit installer
points.text: The Windows build is a 32-bit installer that can install per user or for all users. The Scratch site currently points Windows users to the Microsoft Store while its direct download is paused.

points.title: Older versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 8 versions. macOS needs version 12 or later and lists only the current universal build.
